notes:
I couldn't do the research for Job 36 this time, so there are no notes to give you yet.

I tried to load six pages at once: Enduring Word on Job 36, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Barnes on biblehub.com, and the NET Bible notes. My code crashed before I could read what came back. When I tried again, the tool said I had used up my calls for this turn. So I haven't read a single page.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a link for every point. Notes written from memory would break that, so I haven't written any.

**What I'll do when tools are available again (for example, if you send the request again):**
1. **Main reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, then Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and Barnes on biblehub.com, plus preceptaustin.org and studylight.org.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** For example, whether Elihu is right or wrong, and how vv. 8–15 treat suffering as correction. Sources: John Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Calvin's sermons on Job (ccel.org or monergism.com), Spurgeon (spurgeon.org), Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, Desiring God, Lutheran sites, and Sam Storms.
3. **Other views:**
   - The NET Bible notes on the hard Hebrew in vv. 14, 16–20 and 33.
   - Bible Odyssey on how Elihu's speeches fit the book.
   - Gregory the Great's *Moralia in Job* (newadvent.org or ccel.org) for the Catholic reading.
   - Any prosperity-teaching readings of v. 11 discussed on gotquestions.org or similar sites.

I'll write the notes in your format ("v. 4: …" with a link after each point) and leave out any verse where I find nothing.
